'''Armed conflicts and attacks'''
*[[Colombian conflict]]
**Thirteen [[National Liberation Army (Colombia)|National Liberation Army]] militants and a police lieutenant were killed during a serie of shootouts with [[Colombian Army|soldiers]] and [[National Police of Colombia|police officers]] in [[Bolívar Department|Bolívar]] and [[Arauca Department|Arauca]], [[Colombia]]. Other twelve militants were arrested during the operations.[https://elpublicotv.com/mueren-13-miembros-del-eln-en-enfrentamientos-con-fuerzas-armadas-colombianas/ (El Publico Tv)]
*[[Allied Democratic Forces insurgency]], [[Kivu conflict]]
**Thirteen people are killed, others are [[Kidnapping|kidnapped]] and houses are [[Arson|burned]] by [[Allied Democratic Forces]] gunmen in Mabisu, [[North Kivu]], [[Democratic Republic of the Congo]]. [https://apnews.com/article/islamic-stage-congo-killings-kivu-adf-goma-d054dc1c3a0b43d1439ba83b4075a127 (AP)]

'''Business and economy'''
*The [[Canadian Union of Postal Workers]] go on [[strike action|strike]] after failing to renegotiate their [[contract]] with [[Canada Post]]. [https://apnews.com/article/canada-post-strike-national-mail-service-cupw-mackinnon-b74d2a5c128dc96540e72aa0f170b6b7 (AP)]
*The purchase of conspiracy theory website ''[[InfoWars]]'' to the [[News satire|satirical news content]] maker ''[[The Onion]]'' is put on hold by a [[Texas]] judge after lawyers representing ''InfoWars'' founder [[Alex Jones]] claimed to find irregularities in the auctioning process. ''The Onion'' say they plan to complete their purchase. [https://www.theguardian.com/us-news/2024/nov/15/the-onion-infowars-bankruptcy (''The Guardian'')]

'''Disasters and accidents''' 
*[[2024 Jhansi hospital fire]]
**Ten infants are killed and 16 others are injured in a fire inside a neonatal [[intensive care unit]] at the Jhansi Medical College hospital in [[Jhansi]], [[Uttar Pradesh]], [[North India]]. [https://apnews.com/article/india-jhansi-hospital-fire-newborns-c2236ba37d12e4f5353df5ebb68171e2 (AP)]
*At least ten people are killed in a fire at a retirement residence in [[Villafranca de Ebro]], [[Province of Zaragoza|Zaragoza]], [[Spain]]. [https://www.washingtonpost.com/world/2024/11/15/spain-fire-nursing-home-zaragoza/1141d6b8-a32a-11ef-be87-1106a06524c6_story.html (''The Washington Post'')]

'''International relations'''
*[[Austria–Russia relations]]
**Austrian [[energy company]] [[OMV]] announces, that Russian [[state-owned enterprise|state-owned]] energy company [[Gazprom]] will stop supplying [[natural gas]] to [[Austria]], who receives their natural gas primarily from [[Russia]], starting this weekend. [https://www.dw.com/en/russia-to-stop-supplying-austria-with-natural-gas/a-70798804 (DW)]
*[[Russian invasion of Ukraine]], [[Germany–Russia relations]]
**[[Germany|German]] [[German Chancellor|Chancellor]] [[Olaf Scholz]] holds a telephone call with Russian [[President of Russia|President]] [[Vladimir Putin]] about the [[Russo-Ukrainian war|war]] in [[Ukraine]], their first contact since 2022. Putin tells Scholz that any negotiated settlement to end the war must recognize the [[Russian-occupied territories of Ukraine|territories that Russia has occupied]] as part of [[Russia]] and that [[Ukraine]] must abandon its aspiration to join [[NATO]]. [https://apnews.com/article/scholz-putin-germany-russia-phone-call-f18e42dc5418fb682682d7dae69483a5 (AP)] [https://www.nytimes.com/2024/11/15/world/europe/scholz-putin-russia-germany-call.html (''The New York Times'')]

'''Law and crime'''
*[[2024 Abkhazian protests]]
**Protestors storm the [[People's Assembly of Abkhazia|Parliament of Abkhazia]] in the capital [[Sukhumi]] in opposition to a proposed measure that would allow [[Russians]] to buy property in [[Abkhazia]]. Opposition leader Eshsou Kakalia claims that protestors now control the building. [https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2024/11/15/protesters-storm-parliament-in-breakaway-georgian-region-of-abkhazia (Al Jazeera)]
*[[Assassination of Malcolm X]]
**Three daughters of [[civil rights movement|civil rights]] activist [[Malcolm X]] file a $100 million [[wrongful death claim|wrongful death]] lawsuit against the [[Central Intelligence Agency|CIA]], the [[Federal Bureau of Investigation|FBI]], and the [[New York Police Department]] for their alleged roles in the [[assassination]] of Malcolm X. [https://apnews.com/article/malcolmx-daughters-death-lawsuit-682c71e26cbeaf293d0ea783999c0c5e (AP)]
*[[Gaza war protests]]
**American [[ice cream]] company [[Ben & Jerry's]] sues their parent company [[Unilever]] in a [[United States district court|federal court]] for allegedly [[censorship|censoring]] their statements supporting [[Gaza Strip|Gaza]]. [https://apnews.com/article/ben-jerrys-ice-cream-gaza-unilever-palestinian-8d3d0a378b3f597de0f41b69ca61f339 (AP)] [https://www.businessinsider.com/4-posts-ben-jerrys-parent-company-ordered-not-to-publish-2024-11 (''Business Insider'')]

'''Politics and elections'''
*[[2024 Sri Lankan parliamentary election]]
**[[Sri Lanka]]n [[President of Sri Lanka|President]] [[Anura Kumara Dissanayake]]'s [[National People's Power]] coalition wins a [[supermajority]] in the [[snap election]] for the [[17th Parliament of Sri Lanka]]. [https://www.reuters.com/world/asia-pacific/sri-lankan-presidents-coalition-set-victory-snap-election-2024-11-15/ (Reuters)]
*[[Second presidential transition of Donald Trump]]
**[[President-elect of the United States]] [[Donald Trump]] names [[Karoline Leavitt]] as the [[White House Press Secretary]] for his [[Second presidency of Donald Trump|second term]] in office, which will make her the youngest ever person to serve in the role at 27 years old. [https://apnews.com/article/trump-administration-press-secretary-4c550e04334e87d2075dc6bbe2e244bd (AP)]
*[[President of Kyrgyzstan|Kyrgyzstan President]] [[Sadyr Japarov]] opens the Zhany-Barak village in the [[Osh Region]] of [[Kyrgyzstan]] for resettled residents of the [[Barak, Kyrgyzstan|Barak]] [[Enclave and exclave|exclave]] in [[Uzbekistan]]. [https://24.kg/english/311305_Sadyr_Japarov_participates_in_opening_of_Zhany-Barak_village_in_Osh_region/ (24.kg)]
*[[Prime Minister of Croatia|Croatian Prime Minister]] [[Andrej Plenković]] dismisses [[Ministry of Health (Croatia)|health minister]] [[Vili Beroš]] on suspicions of [[corruption]]. [https://www.dw.com/en/croatian-pm-fires-health-minister-amid-corruption-scandal/a-70786764 (DW)]
